title: External memory is the durable working state
summary: Use external versioned records across sessions. Show current active rules, current checkpoint and linked module detail; keep dated history without loading it all. Preserve older rules that still apply.
body: The record graph is versioned JSON; SQLite is a rebuildable search index. Use expected_revision to reject stale writes. Do not edit prior revisions. Exact agreement snapshots and old plans remain retrievable. Latest user instructions override older records; save that override instead of silently obeying stale state. Each important observation belongs in a timestamped local event or versioned record. A new instruction does not silently erase an older applicable one: record whether it adds to, narrows or supersedes that rule, and update the active version explicitly. A timestamp alone establishes sequence, not authority. Raw events survive new sessions in this folder but are ignored by Git; durable cross-machine conclusions need committed records.
change_reason: Clarify temporal history versus current active memory
